summary:
These numbers are ESTIMATES built from published averages. They are not quotes, and real quotes in Madison can vary by 30-50% between insurers.

METHOD. Price = Madison baseline x vehicle factor (VF) x car-age factor x driver multiplier x coverage factor.
(1) Madison baseline for full coverage is $1,935/yr: Insure.com, 40-year-old, clean record, 100/300/100 limits, $500 deductible. It is about 5% below the WI average of $2,026. The minimum-coverage baseline is $476/yr: the mean of MoneyGeek Madison $432, Bankrate WI $456, NerdWallet WI $554 and ValuePenguin WI $540, with the state figures scaled by 0.95 for Madison.
(2) VF = The Zebra's 6-month full-coverage price for the model divided by its national average of $1,162. Results: RAV4 0.74, Highlander 0.80, LR4 0.815, Camry and Corolla 0.82, IS 250 0.85, Prius 0.85, RX 0.885, GX 460 (stand-in for the GX 470) 0.88, ES 0.94, Evoque 1.02, Range Rover Sport 1.24.
(3) The car-age factor (0.72-0.90) is my own estimate. It rests on MoneyGeek's model-year data (for example, an RX 350 costs $123/mo for a 2018 vs $227 for a 2025) and ValuePenguin's finding that premiums fall about 11-13% for every 5 years of car age.
(4) Driver multiplier vs a 40-year-old comes from Bankrate's age table (age 22 $4,543, 25 $3,326, 30 $2,877, 40 about $2,697). Profile (a) uses 1.10 / 1.35 / 1.68 for ages 28 / 24 / 22. Profile (b) uses 1.4 / 1.9 / 2.6: the age factor times a surcharge of 1.26 to 1.53 for having no US history. The 1.26 is from Insurify (new international driver pays $236 vs $187 average for full coverage). The 1.53 is from ValuePenguin (someone first licensed at 25 pays 53% more).
(5) Coverage factor: 0.80 for 50/100/50 with a $1,000 deductible, 0.90 for 100/300/100 with $1,000, 1.00 for 100/300/100 with $500.

TYPICAL ANNUAL PRICE, before discounts.
Profile (a), full coverage:
- RAV4 about $1,430, Highlander $1,470, GX 470 $1,560
- RX 350 $1,620, Camry $1,640, Corolla $1,650
- Prius $1,700, ES 350 $1,720, LR4 $1,720, IS 250 AWD $1,790
- Evoque $1,910, Range Rover Sport $2,100
Profile (a), WI minimum: about $600-670/yr.
Profile (b): about 1.4x profile (a). Full coverage runs from $2,010 (RAV4) to $2,950 (Range Rover Sport); minimum is about $840-950.
For the 10.5 months you'll own the car (Oct to mid-Aug, with a pro-rata refund), multiply by 0.875. Profile (a) full coverage comes to about $1,250-1,840; profile (b) about $1,760-2,580.

Takeaway: the driver profile moves the price much more than the car. Across brands, the gap for profile (a) full coverage is only about $700/yr (RAV4/Highlander cheapest, Range Rover Sport most expensive). A 2010-2014 Lexus ES or RX costs about the same to insure as a Camry.

WI REQUIREMENTS. Liability 25/50/10 plus uninsured motorist 25/50 are mandatory. Underinsured motorist is optional, with at least 50/100 limits if you buy it. Insurers must offer medical payments of at least $1,000, but you may reject it. Wisconsin has no PIP.

FOREIGN LICENSE / INTERNATIONAL STUDENT. WisDOT lets students from countries in the Geneva Convention (or the Inter-American Convention) drive on their home license for up to 1 year. Mainland China is party to neither the 1949 Geneva nor the 1968 Vienna convention, so a PRC license holder should plan to get a WI license. Taiwan, South Korea, France and Germany have reciprocity, which can waive the tests. Insurers that write foreign-license drivers include Progressive (online quote with an IDP), State Farm (accepts them, but by agent only), GEICO, Farmers, Dairyland and Bristol West. Erie agents are reportedly familiar with foreign licenses. I found no published policy for American Family (based in Madison), so ask an agent. USAA is military families only. Expect a no-US-history surcharge.

DISCOUNTS. Good student: up to 25% at State Farm, up to 15% at GEICO, about 7.5% on average at Progressive; usually requires being under 25 with a B average (3.0 GPA). Telematics: State Farm Drive Safe & Save gives up to 30% and never raises the rate; AmFam KnowYourDrive gives up to 15% and doesn't raise it; Progressive Snapshot raises rates for about 20% of drivers. Pay-in-full, paperless and renters bundling give smaller savings; policy-related discounts are typically 5-25%. Shopping around matters a lot: in MoneyGeek's Madison data, GEICO full coverage is $568/yr vs a $1,008 city average.

IS FULL COVERAGE WORTH IT? For a $10-13k car, Wisconsin's deer risk is high:
- WisDOT counted 17,795 deer crashes in 2025, 792 of them in Dane County (4th in the state).
- State Farm puts Wisconsin odds at 1 in 62, 3rd-worst in the US, with November, October and December the peak months.
- Deer claims average about $3,000 (Triple-I) and up to $5,620 in high-risk areas (AAA, 2024). Hitting a deer is covered by comprehensive, not collision.

Recommendation:
- Always carry comprehensive. It costs roughly 10% of a liability premium (ValuePenguin), about $60-100/yr for profile (a). My rough expected deer loss alone is about 1/62 x $3,000-5,600 = $50-90/yr per car, before theft, hail and glass.
- Add collision with a $1,000 deductible unless you could absorb losing the whole $10-13k car. This matters especially for profile (b) and for a first Wisconsin winter.
- Adding comp and collision costs about $780-1,420/yr for (a) and $1,100-2,000/yr for (b), roughly 6-15% of the car's value per year. That is under ValuePenguin's rule of thumb for dropping the coverage (car worth less than about 10x the yearly full-coverage cost).
- Use liability of at least 50/100/50, preferably 100/300/100, plus UIM. The state minimum's $10k property-damage limit is low.

CANCELLING MID-TERM. Wisconsin rule Ins 6.10(4) says an insurer may refund less than pro rata only if it gave you a separate written notice of a "substantial penalty," and only 10 or more days after that notice. Cancellations the insurer starts, or that happen for nonpayment, must be refunded pro rata. State Farm refunds pro rata (7-14 business days). Progressive is mostly pro rata, with some short-rate cases. GEICO charges no fee outside North Carolina. A short-rate penalty is typically about 10% of the unused premium. Plan: get "pro-rata" confirmed in writing, use 6-month terms or monthly payments (or pay in full only once pro rata is confirmed), and cancel effective on the day the title transfers in August 2027.

Uncertainty band: roughly ±30%, driven by insurer, credit-based insurance score, exact ZIP and trim. Get 5-6 quotes: GEICO, Progressive, State Farm, American Family, Erie and Travelers (NerdWallet's cheapest WI full coverage, $991/yr).

facts.item: Wisconsin rule for driving on a foreign license
facts.value: Students from countries party to the Geneva Convention (or the Inter-American convention) may drive on a valid home license for up to 1 year; an IDP or English translation is advised. Students from countries party to neither 'may be required to obtain a driver license' on arrival.

Mainland China is not party to the 1949 Geneva or 1968 Vienna road-traffic conventions and cannot issue an official IDP. A PRC license holder therefore likely cannot rely on the WI 1-year rule and should get a WI license (knowledge and road tests).
facts.notes: Applying this to WI is my inference. Confirm with UW ISS (iss.wisc.edu/students/current-students/drivers-license/).

facts.value: License holders from France, Germany, South Korea and Taiwan may have the WI knowledge and skills tests waived

Progressive: online quotes with an IDP. State Farm: accepts foreign licenses but quotes only by phone or agent. GEICO, Farmers, Dairyland and Bristol West also write them. Erie agents are reportedly familiar, but availability varies. American Family: no published policy found, so ask a Madison agent. USAA: military families only. Most add a surcharge because they can't verify your driving history.

facts.item: Odds of an animal collision in Wisconsin (State Farm, Jul 2025-Jun 2026)
facts.value: 1 in 62, 3rd-highest in the US after West Virginia (1 in 46) and Montana (1 in 54). National odds are 1 in 145. Peak months are November, October and December.

Triple-I puts the average at about $3,000; AAA East Central reported $5,620 in high-risk areas in 2024. Animal strikes are paid under comprehensive, not collision. My rough estimate of the expected yearly deer loss per WI car is 1/62 x $3,000-5,620 = about $50-90.

facts.item: When full coverage stops being worth it
facts.value: Consider dropping comp/collision when the car is worth less than about 10x the yearly full-coverage cost, or 4-6 years of comp/collision premium (typically cars 8-12 years old worth $5-10k). Comprehensive costs about 10% as much as a liability-only policy; collision costs about as much as liability-only.

facts.item: Wisconsin rule on refunds when you cancel (Wis. Admin. Code Ins 6.10(4))
facts.value: An insurer may refund less than the pro-rata unearned premium only if it gave a separate written notice that you may pay a 'substantial penalty' for cancelling early, and only 10 or more days after that notice. Refunds must be pro rata when the insurer cancels or cancels for nonpayment.
facts.applies_to: Cancelling when you sell in Aug 2027

facts.value: State Farm: no fee, pro-rata refund within 7-14 business days. Progressive: no flat fee and mostly pro-rata, but some mid-term cancellations use short-rate. GEICO: no fee except short-rate in North Carolina. A short-rate penalty is usually about 10% of the unused premium.
